post.description:
A link to /storefiles?files=<files> that passes the login check once without the cookie.

For browsers that hand a download to a helper without the cookie (Android's sign-in window). It works once, for
600 seconds, from this browser's address, for these files only.

get.description:
nginx's auth_request: may this browser have X-Original-URI, which needs X-TM-Required-Role?

Only nginx's internal /_auth locations call verify, and only they set X-TM-Required-Role (viewer or admin);
nginx refuses the path from the network and clears the header on /api/. Any other call gets 404 and no identity.
401 with X-TM-Redirect sends the browser to /setup, /login?next=..., /welcome (an admin, while a new license
agreement waits), or /waiting (a viewer, meanwhile). 403 is forbidden.
200 carries X-TM-User, X-TM-Role, X-TM-Frigate-Secret, and for admins X-TM-NR-Token.
Without a session, a good download link (POST /download-link) passes once: 200 with X-TM-User and X-TM-Role only,
no other secret and no cookie. A login redirect's next= leaves the link's token out.

post.description: End every session of the current user, in every browser, including this one.

get.description: What the UI needs to pick a page. Never 401: without a session, user is null.

Also the device's home-page theme, so the setup and login pages use its colors before anyone logs in, and, when
the page came over the hotspot (nginx sets X-TM-Hotspot to exactly 1), the name an iPhone can open outside it.

post.description: Create the first admin with the setup code tmsetup printed, accept the EULA for them, and log them in.
An admin accepts a new EULA version for the device, which lets everyone back into the apps.
Change one's own password. Ends the user's other sessions; this browser gets a new cookie and stays in.

Set another user's password and end their sessions. Admins change their own on the account page, which asks
for the current password, so a session left open can't be used to take the account over.
Start the job that writes the secret and restarts what reads it.

delete.description:
Start the job that empties the secret's file and restarts what reads it. For one not set, the job still writes
the empty value and its env lines and restarts the units.

put.description:
Stream the body into model_cache as a model file, a sidecar (<model>.json), or an archive. `:path` lets a name
with a slash reach the name check, which refuses it.

post.description: Write <name>.json for a model file that has none, for the device's detector.

get.description:
The model's file, its sidecar, and SHA256SUMS in a zip, as an attachment named <name>.zip: only for a model
with both halves, which a default never has. GET /models/{name}/file sends any model's file alone.

The model's file alone, as an attachment under its own name, whether or not it has a sidecar: the download for
a model with none to package, such as a default, or a file whose details were never filled in.

delete.description:
Remove the model's file and its sidecar, whichever are there, unless Frigate runs it or it's a default.
What runs is Frigate's answer, or config.yml's when Frigate doesn't answer; when neither can say, nothing is
removed.

post.description:
Put back what the installer gives this device: its Coral model for an edgetpu detector, and otherwise no
`model:` section, so Frigate runs its own default. Declared before /{name}/use, so `default` names no model.

Make Frigate run a model in model_cache that has its file and sidecar and is built for the device's detector.
A default's file (the installer's, or Frigate's own) is the default, as POST /models/default/use puts it back. The
running model may be used again: Frigate just restarts.

get.description:
The places, after the store and config.yml are brought into step. Node-RED not answering isn't an error here:
the places are listed with no counts and `nodered` false.

put.description:
Write database_precision into config.yml (Node-RED re-rounds the open rows to a coarser one), and with
round_stored also lower every row already stored.

post.description:
Check a CSV of planned places (description,lat,lon, then a column per sensor holding its bearing) and, unless
dry_run, create them all, or none when any line is refused (422 with the problems in detail).

patch.description: Edit a planned place (409 not_planned for one in use or used: correct those instead).

delete.description: Delete a place and its corrections (409 in_use for the place in use). Node-RED's rows keep its id.

post.description:
Put the place in use: its id, point, and each enabled sensor's bearing into config.yml (a sensor the body leaves
out takes the place's stored bearing, else the file's), then wait for Node-RED to start the deployments.

Node-RED not answering isn't an error: the file is written, and `reloaded` is false.

get.description: How many events the place's deployments recorded, and when the first and last began.

post.description:
Correct where a used or in-use place was: the store (with a correction row), config.yml for the place in use,
and Node-RED's rows, re-rounded to the precision each was stored at. A 502 means the store and the file changed
and the rows didn't; correcting again with the same pair re-rounds them.

Correct which way one deployment's sensor faced. For an open deployment of the place in use, the place's bearing
and config.yml's change too, after Node-RED's row, so Node-RED doesn't start a new deployment. Refused (502) while
Node-RED doesn't answer (decision 12).
